coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offsets and VAs.

function.note: GNU objdump prints this window under a nearest-symbol label with a tens-of-megabytes offset; that is stripped-binary arithmetic, not an identity, and no source-level function is claimed from it.

behavior.arguments: edi = value returned for in-range bytes; esi = value selected/transformed for out-of-range bytes; only the low byte of edi (al) is read
behavior.select_rule: b = edi & 0xff; if 0xc0 <= b < 0xe0: return edi; elif b == 0: return esi; elif b <= 0x8f: return (esi & 0xffffff00) | ((esi & 0x0f) | 0x80); elif b == 0x90: return (esi & 0xffffff00) | ((esi & 0x0f) | 0x90); elif b == 0xa0: return (esi & 0xffffff00) | ((esi & 0x1f) | 0xa0); else: return esi

edges.upper_bytes: transform cases modify only the low byte of esi; the upper 24 bits of esi pass through, and in-range returns carry the full 32-bit edi

behavior.scout_correction: The round-5 scout note described this window as 'if the low byte of edi lies in [0xc0, 0xe0) return esi, else return edi'. The retained bytes show the opposite direction plus five further branches: in-range bytes return edi unchanged, and out-of-range bytes return esi, transformed in three byte classes (b <= 0x8f, b == 0x90, b == 0xa0) and unchanged otherwise. The scout note also gave the FDE end as 0x359bebd; the FDE record ends at 0x359bebe (the ret at 0x359bebd is one byte). The scout's 'unreachable branch' remark is true only in the narrow sense that the 0x8f/0x90/0xa0 branches are never reached for in-range bytes; for out-of-range bytes they are the body of the function and are fully reachable.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan for e8 rel32 targeting 0x359be70 anywhere in .text; explicitly not a complete xref census. Only the first three sites were confirmed as instruction starts by linear disassembly from their caller FDE starts; the remaining sites are scan results, not individually confirmed instruction starts.

caller_fdes.note: both sites confirmed as instruction starts by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start
